Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

bomb noun

also bombs, explosive, atom bomb, atomic bomb, nuclear bomb, bombing, bomb (verb), go off, explode, bomber

modern

Traupman 186, 281
M-O s.v. bomb (Bartal)

bomba, bombae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a bomb

Traupman’s word, from Italian bomba: bomba atomica, bomba nucleāris (Traupman 186). Classical bombus is a booming or humming sound, not a bomb.

Other words

  • pyrobolus, pyrobolī m. — a bomb; an explosive shell

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. bomb (Egger) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Egger’s word (from Greek): pyrobolus atomicus, an atom bomb; pyrobolus subterrāneus, a land mine (M-O s.v. mine).

  • bombīs oppugnāre — to bomb (a place)

    also used · modern · Traupman 186

    Egger says pyrobolīs verberāre (M-O s.v. bomb).

  • displōdō, displōdere, —, displōsum — set off, explode; passive, go off

    verb, third conjugation · also used · modern · M-O s.v. detonate (Egger); Lucr. 6.131 (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Egger’s sense: pyrobolus erat displōsus, the bomb had gone off (M-O s.v. explode). Classically, to spread out, and in the participle “burst apart”, of a bladder (Lucr. 6.131).

Examples

  • āëroplanum bombiferum

    a bomberTraupman 186

See also weapon, war, gun.
